text:
marta_csm: heads-up 1 Squall just finished their private/VPC cutover. most services healthy but they reported a ~14m hole in audit logs for egress to external APIs. flagging infra + security to triage :mag:
diego_net: can you share which AZ/subnet and whether they used a TGW or simple peering?
marta_csm: they used vpc-peering sparq-squall->redwood-priv-vpc, edge-subnet-b2, customer NAT gateway in their account. hole aligns with a traffic surge at ~14:05 UTC.
ryan_platform: quick check 1 our forwarder returned 403 on S3 PutObject. error in our logs: "AccessDenied: Access Denied" and KMS returned "NotAuthorizedException" when trying to encrypt. looks like the CMK is in the customer's account and they didn't grant use to our forwarder role.
safiya_security: saw the same in CloudTrail: KMS:GenerateDataKeyWithoutPlaintext denied for principal arn:aws:sts::987654321098:assumed-role/redwood-forwarder/instance. customer key policy only allows their account root and one IAM role.
diego_net: network checks are clean; packets reached our edge. not a connectivity issue.
marta_csm: customer notes: "we don't want to widen key policy; can you recommend a least-priv approach?" they are worried about key explosion and rotation governance.
safiya_security: recommend a KMS grant rather than broad key policy edits - grant scoped to our forwarder principal and only for Encrypt/GenerateDataKey. it's auditable and revokable without key policy churn. sample CLI to create a grant for them:
```
aws kms create-grant --key-id alias/squall-logs --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::987654321098:role/redwood-forwarder --operations Encrypt GenerateDataKey --name "RedwoodForwarderGrant"
```
this avoids changing the key policy and preserves their rotation settings.
ryan_platform: once they create the grant, we should retry a small canary to validate. plan: schedule canary immediately after they confirm grant.
diego_net: also ask them to enable S3 server access logs and set a short lifecycle on the access logs bucket so we can confirm ingestion without leaving data forever.
marta_csm: scheduling a 15m sync with Squall's infra in 20m. can @diego_net and @safiya_security join?
safiya_security: I can join and walk them through the grant flow and check CloudTrail rejections in realtime.
dryan_platform: small note: if they insist on not granting cross-account, fallback is to let them send logs to an intermediate bucket in their account with a short-term role we assume. that's more operational overhead, so prefer grant.
marta_csm: customer asked about whether this affects their renewal or SLA. preliminary risk = "monitoring" not yet high. if logs remain missing >24h we'll escalate to "medium".
safiya_security: agree. remediating with a grant should be low effort. also documenting a short one-pager for customers on "KMS grants vs key policy" would help. can we add that to onboarding assets?
ryan_platform: I'll add a sample playbook and a one-slide visual explaining grant vs policy tradeoffs.
deploy-bot: canary-deploy(squall-forwarder) scheduled at 6145554365  status: pending
marta_csm: update 1 customer created grant and shared GrantToken id. joining call now to validate.
deploy-bot: canary-deploy(squall-forwarder) completed at 6145554372  status: success
dryan_platform: canary successful 1 S3 200 and KMS Encrypt calls succeeded.
diego_net: correlated VPC flow logs: no drops during canary window. good to close the gap.
safiya_security: CloudTrail shows no KMS denies after grant. I'll follow up with a short audit checklist (grant id, creation time, who created).
marta_csm: closing the loop with Squall, adding the one-pager action to onboarding repo (owner: ryan_platform). renewal_risk: set back to "low"; will monitor 24h for any regressions. thanks team :sparkles:
